cases.prompt: Set up an A/B test on the pricing page to detect a 5% lift in signups.
cases.setup: Baseline conversion is 2%. Traffic is about 40,000 eligible users per month.
expect_pass: computes the required sample of roughly 315,000 per arm and translates it to about thirteen months at this traffic
returns the verdict that the test cannot answer this question, rather than designing a shorter version
gives the levers with concrete numbers: a 20% MDE needs about 21,000 per arm and runs in roughly three weeks
offers the higher-baseline sub-population and the more sensitive proxy outcome as alternatives, naming what each costs in generalisation
makes a recommendation rather than listing options, and justifies it
expect_fail: designs a two-week test and notes it may be underpowered
reports the required sample without a go or no-go verdict

cases.prompt: The test came back not significant. So the new onboarding flow doesn't work — kill it?
cases.setup: Effect +3.1%, interval -2% to +8.4%. The test was powered to detect 9%.
expect_pass: corrects the reading: the test could not detect an effect of 9% or larger, and a 6% effect would have looked like this result
reports the interval and notes it spans zero and extends to 8.4%, so effects worth having remain possible
distinguishes this from a decisive null, and says explicitly that this result does not support killing the flow
names what a conclusive test would take in sample or duration
does not claim the flow works either
expect_fail: agrees the flow does not work
reports only non-significance with no interval or MDE

cases.prompt: Variant B is up 7%. Ship it.
cases.setup: Arms split 54/46 against an intended 50/50, at a sample size where that is far outside chance. The imbalance grows with funnel depth.
expect_pass: refuses to read the outcome and identifies the sample-ratio mismatch as invalidating
explains why: assignment was not random, so the outcome difference is confounded with whatever caused the imbalance
uses the funnel-depth pattern to name a likely cause, such as assignment being logged after a step that differs between arms
explicitly declines to report the 7% as a result while disclosing that it was observed
notes the design and power calculation remain valid for a re-run
expect_fail: reports the 7% lift with an SRM caveat

cases.prompt: We've been watching daily and it just crossed significance on day 6 of a planned 14-day test. Can we stop?
expect_pass: says stopping now is not valid under a fixed-horizon design and explains why in one sentence: each look is another chance to cross, so the realised false-positive rate is far above 5%
states that switching to a sequential method now does not retroactively fix peeking already done
recommends running to the planned horizon, and notes that if the effect is real it will still be there
distinguishes health monitoring, which is required, from primary-outcome monitoring with intent to stop
if the result is reported anyway, requires the peeking to be disclosed and the result treated as a hypothesis for a clean re-run
expect_fail: approves stopping because significance was reached
suggests applying a sequential correction after the fact as though it repairs the design

cases.prompt: We randomised by lead and want to report the effect on account conversion rate.
expect_pass: flags the unit mismatch: multiple leads per account are correlated, so treating accounts as independent understates variance
names the consequence directionally: results look more significant than they are
states the correct design, randomising by account, and acknowledges it costs sample size
offers the analysis options available now: analyse at lead level as randomised, or use a cluster-robust method at account level, naming the assumption each makes
does not report a naive account-level significance test
expect_fail: reports account-level significance from lead-level randomisation
declares the test worthless with no salvageable analysis

cases.prompt: Overall flat, but mobile-tablet users are up 14%. Can we ship to that segment?
cases.setup: Eleven segment cuts were examined. No correction was applied and no segment was pre-registered.
expect_pass: states the family size and gives the arithmetic: across eleven cuts at alpha 0.05, at least one false positive was more likely than not
labels the segment result exploratory, explicitly and in the same sentence as the number
does not simply dismiss it: frames it as a hypothesis worth a dedicated pre-registered test if the mechanism is plausible
notes that the overall flat result is the pre-registered finding and is what governs the shipping decision
offers the correction that would apply if a formal answer is needed
expect_fail: reports the 14% without the family size

cases.prompt: Set up A/B tests across our email, push and SMS campaigns and report results from one place.
expect_pass: states that Iterable's experiment metrics endpoint supports email experiments only, so push, SMS and in-app tests have no metrics endpoint
does not imply parity across channels
requires the non-email measurement route to be established before launch, through the warehouse or event pipeline
notes that a readout route discovered after the test has run is an unrecoverable problem
still designs the tests, with the measurement plan differing by channel and that difference stated
expect_fail: promises a unified multichannel experiment readout from the platform

cases.prompt: Variant A won on conversion rate. Write it up.
cases.setup: Variant B launched one day later than variant A, so its measurement window is one day shorter.
expect_pass: applies the comparison contract before reading the result and catches the window mismatch
states that equal window length is not equal coverage and that the arms are not comparable as measured
gives the correction: restrict both arms to the common window and recompute
reports the recomputed comparison rather than only objecting
notes that a winner declared from mismatched definitions survives every statistical check, which is why the contract runs first
expect_fail: writes up variant A as the winner on the mismatched windows
invalidates the test without offering the common-window recomputation
